summary: Medtech lobbyist AdvaMed called for the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to make more devices eligible for a proposed pathway to faster Medicare coverage. The CMS unveiled plans for the pathway earlier this year, which would give certain breakthrough devices a proposed national coverage determination upon Food and Drug Administration authorization. AdvaMed praised the pathway earlier this year as a “positive step” toward expanding access to breakthrough devices, but called for clearer timelines and broader eligibility. The CMS is accepting public comments on the program through Oct. 13.
title: Medtech lobby seeks broader device eligibility for CMS’ proposed RAPID pathway

summary: Healthcare organizations aren’t prepared for cybersecurity threats from quantum computing — an emerging technology that could break the encryption protecting patient data — according to a new report. Medical devices lag behind traditional information technology systems in preparedness. Just 6% of medical devices have security that can withstand future quantum computer attacks, compared with 50% of IT systems, according to the report by cybersecurity company Forescout’s threat intelligence and research arm. Electronic medical records, medical imaging and lab results are the data types most at risk. Experts say healthcare leaders should address these risks sooner rather than later.
title: Healthcare organizations are underprepared for quantum computing threats

summary: MMI said Thursday it raised $125 million in a Series D financing to expand access to its robotic microsurgery system in the U.S. as well as key global markets. The Symani robotic system is designed for soft tissue open surgery, allowing surgeons to repair tiny structures such as lymphatic vessels and nerves. The robot filters out tremors while translating the surgeon’s hand and wrist motions into robotic movement of its miniaturized instruments. MMI also plans to use the new funds to generate more clinical evidence for robotic microsurgery, including in the REMIND clinical trial evaluating the robot’s use in people with Alzheimer’s disease.
title: MMI raises $125M to scale up in robotic microsurgery

summary: Fitzgerald will oversee three newly established reportable segments as Boston Scientific works to bounce back from guidance cuts.
title: Boston Scientific names Joseph Fitzgerald as chief operating officer

summary: Kurz’s appointment comes as Medtronic enjoys strong growth in electrophysiology therapies thanks to demand for its pulsed field ablation devices.
title: Medtronic names Felicia Kurz as cardiac ablation VP, GM

summary: The U.K.’s medical products regulator on Tuesday backed recommendations related to artificial intelligence in healthcare, emphasizing the continuous monitoring of AI-enabled devices. The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency adopted all 44 recommendations made by the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare, an independent group led by National Health Service physicians. One of the commission’s key conclusions was that AI-enabled medical devices’ performance should be monitored throughout their working life, rather than through one-time assessments. The decision comes as other entities, including the Food and Drug Administration, are also considering postmarket monitoring as a regulatory approach.
title: UK backs continuous oversight of AI medical devices

summary: Abbott received Food and Drug Administration approval for updates to its heart monitoring implant that allow patients to be more involved in their care. The company’s CardioMEMS device, first approved in 2014, is a small sensor implanted in the pulmonary artery to measure pulmonary artery pressure and send notifications of worsening heart failure. The updates will allow patients to view their pulmonary artery pressure readings for the first time and receive personalized medication updates through a smartphone app, Abbott said Monday.
title: Abbott gets FDA nod for updates to heart failure monitoring system

summary: A U.S. district court has ordered Apple to pay Masimo $184.2 million in interest on the damages a jury awarded last year. The interest covers the $634 million in damages that a jury ordered Apple to pay Masimo one year ago. Apple received the order because its Apple Watch product infringed a pulse oximetry patent. A judge for the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California sided with Masimo in a ruling on interest Monday, bringing the total Apple needs to pay to more than $818 million. Danaher bought Masimo for $9.9 billion in June.
title: Apple ordered to pay Masimo $184M in interest on patent damages

summary: Zenflow said Monday it has raised $52 million and partnered with Cook Medical to facilitate the commercialization of a urology device. The agreements support the Zenflow Spring system, a treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia that received Food and Drug Administration approval in December. Zenflow’s device has a different design from the BPH treatments offered by Boston Scientific, Olympus and Teleflex to bridge the gap between medicines and more invasive procedures.
title: Zenflow raises $52M, inks distribution deal with Cook Medical

summary: Stryker CEO Kevin Lobo will step down after more than 15 years at the company, according to a Tuesday announcement. Lobo will become executive chair of Stryker’s board of directors starting on Jan. 1. Spencer Stiles, Stryker’s current chief operating officer, will become its next CEO, also joining the board. Stiles, 50, has nearly 30 years of experience at Stryker “spanning leadership roles across virtually every business,” RBC Capital Markets analyst Kendall Au wrote in a research note. Stiles also has a close working relationship with Lobo.
title: Stryker CEO Kevin Lobo to resign
